subject: Proposal: phased activation + GPU cost-sharing staircase for Nimbus Labs
body:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Chen <alan@nimbuslabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: phased activation + GPU cost-sharing staircase for Nimbus Labs

Alan,

Thanks for the time yesterday. Attached is a compact proposal for the Reserved Capacity commitment we discussed — the key idea is a phased activation schedule combined with a GPU cost-sharing "staircase" (index-triggered pass-through with capped exposures and an executive credit ladder).

Summary (TL;DR):
- Commit: 1.8PB-hr per year equivalent (reserved SKU mix: A100/RTX mix) with 18-month term.
- Phasing: three activation slices (30% immediate, +40% at month 6, +30% at month 12) to align with your ramp and limit stranded capacity.
- GPU index trigger: if our benchmarked market index (Redwood GPU Index) moves >15% above baseline, a temporary pass-through surcharge up to a capped band applies; if >30% we escalate to an exec credit review.
- Discount staircase: base discount is applied upfront; additional one-time credit tiers unlock if index breaches certain thresholds during the first 12 months (see attached cost-sensitivity model).

Why this helps Nimbus:
- Limits early over-provisioning for your initial pilot workloads.
- Preserves long-term pricing protection but shares short-term market shocks to avoid extreme margin compression for Redwood.

Ask: please review the attached plan and the cost-sensitivity workbook. We need feedback on three items by EOD Tue 27 Apr: (1) acceptable activation dates for slice 2 and 3, (2) the maximum pass-through cap you are comfortable with (we propose 20%), (3) confirmation that a 18-month term aligns with internal procurement cycles.

Attachments referenced: nimbus-phased-plan-v1.pdf (proposal), cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx (scenario tabbed).

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

----
From: Alan Chen <alan@nimbuslabs.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased activation + GPU cost-sharing staircase for Nimbus Labs

Marcus —

Appreciate the write-up. A few clarifying questions before we loop legal/procurement:
1) The pass-through cap you propose (20%) — is that on the token/unit price only or the total monthly invoice?
2) Can you provide a simple example scenario: say the index spikes 40% in Q2 due to a supply outage; what would Nimbus see on months 1–3 under your model?
3) We prefer a 24-month contract window from procurement standpoint. Is Redwood open to a longer term if we agree to a slightly higher initial commit?

I'll ping contracts and legal once we have those answers.

Thanks,
Alan Chen
Director of Infrastructure, Nimbus Labs
alan@nimbuslabs.ai

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposal: phased activation + GPU cost-sharing staircase for Nimbus Labs

Internal notes / suggested edits for Marcus' reply to Alan: 
- Clarify cap semantics: pass-through cap applies to incremental GPU surcharge portion of the invoice (we don't retroactively index the base recurring fees).
- Sample scenario: include a worked example in the workbook that shows month-by-month invoice with and without surcharge, and the executive credit ladder step-up.
- Term flexibility: propose 18 -> 24 month flex: if Nimbus moves to 24 months, increase reserved commitment by +12% and reduce base price by 2 percentage points.
- Approval path: any >25% pass-through exposure requires VP Sales + VP Finance sign-off; >40% triggers an executive-level review and potential one-time credit.

I'll draft the sample scenario table and add a worksheet to the model. Karthik — ops constraints noted below.

-Marissa
VP, Strategic Deals | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposal: phased activation + GPU cost-sharing staircase for Nimbus Labs

Ops perspective:
- Lead times: provisioning new reserved capacity (non-burst) needs ~8–12 weeks to schedule in our next tranche given current fleet utilization. If slice 2 is month 6, we must lock the activation trigger at month 4 to meet provisioning windows.
- Burstable overlay: recommend enabling a controlled burst overlay (short-term on-demand buffer) for months when index triggers until reserved capacity can be turned on — this reduces customer impact while we provision. Charge for burst at on-demand rates with monthly cap; this should be lower than full pass-through.
- Monitoring & runbook: we need a joint ops runbook and an SLA for activation acknowledgements. Suggest a 48-hour notification SLA for activation requests and a 10-business-day escalation path if provisioning slips.

I'll sync with Infrastructure to map the exact dates once Alan confirms preferred activation months.

-Karthik
Head of Dedicated Ops | Redwood Inference

----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Chen <alan@nimbuslabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, contracts@nimbuslabs.ai, legal@nimbuslabs.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased activation + GPU cost-sharing staircase for Nimbus Labs

Alan —

Thanks for the questions. Short answers up-front, full workbook now updated and attached.

1) Cap semantics: the pass-through cap applies to the incremental surcharge line only (not the base reserved invoice). We've added a month-by-month worked example to the workbook showing both the incremental surcharge line and net amount due.

2) 40% spike example: see "Scenario Q2-SupplyShock" tab in cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx. In that scenario (40% index increase):
   - Month 1: surcharge hits 20% cap -> incremental surcharge billed at 20% (capped)
   - Month 2: index still elevated -> surcharge continues at cap; we apply a one-time mitigation credit of 7% to Month 2 invoice (per the executive credit ladder)
   - Month 3: if index remains >30% after two months, we escalate to VP review and may implement an additional ad hoc credit (per approval path).

3) Term: Redwood is open to 24 months if Nimbus increases committed capacity by 12% and accepts a 2pp reduction in base price. I've added a comparison table under the "Term Flex" tab.

Next steps we propose:
- You and procurement review the updated workbook and SOW draft (attached: sow-draft-nimbus.docx).
- Contracts/legal loop for cleanroom review — I CC'd both.
- Tentative call to finalize the SOW and activation dates: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 at 10:00 AM PT. I'll send a calendar invite.

DocuSign & HubSpot: I've pushed a draft SOW to DocuSign (link below) and created the deal record in HubSpot.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/xyz-embedded-link
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/DBL-2027-0139

Attachments included: nimbus-phased-plan-v1.pdf (proposal), cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx (worked scenarios), sow-draft-nimbus.docx (SOW draft).

Looking forward — please confirm the 29 Apr slot or propose alternatives.

Best,
Marcus
Head of Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
